lessons.title: Planning a dashboard people will use
KPI cards with formulas
lessons.mac:
• ⌘ + 1 > Custom > Type
• ▲ ▼: Control + ⌘ + Space (Character Viewer), search 'triangle'
• Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules

steps.say: Before anyone reads a chart, they look for three numbers: how much we sold, whether we grew, and whether we hit target. These KPI cards answer that at a glance, with green and red arrows that change by themselves.
You will learn to build a revenue card, a growth card with an arrow, and a target card that turns red when you fall short. Practice sheet S17-02.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. A revenue card with SUM
2. A growth card with an arrow number format
3. A target card with conditional formatting

Practice: sheet S17-02

steps.say: A KPI card is a label, one big number, and a comparison. The arrows come from a custom number format with three parts: one for positive numbers, one for negative, one for zero. Colours can live in the format too.

acts.t:
Arrow number format

[Color10]▲ 0.0%;[Red]▼ 0.0%;0.0%
 positive   ;  negative  ; zero

[Color10] = green · [Red] = red
The minus sign is replaced by ▼, so -4.2% shows as ▼ 4.2%

steps.say: Our data has monthly revenue for last year, this year and this year's target. The cards sit to the right, in F3, H3 and J3.
In F3, type equals SUM, open bracket, C2 colon C13, close bracket, and press Return. Revenue for the year is thirteen crore sixty-three lakh rupees.
In H3, the growth: equals SUM of C2 to C13, divided by SUM of B2 to B13, minus one. Press Return.
Here is the common mistake: leaving it like this. Zero point one zero three means nothing to a busy reader. Select H3, press Command 1, choose Custom, and type the arrow format. Click OK.
In J3, target achieved: equals SUM of C2 to C13 divided by SUM of D2 to D13. It shows one hundred and two point six percent.
Make it turn red below target. With J3 selected, choose Home, Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Less Than. Type one, keep Light Red Fill with Dark Red Text, and click OK.

acts.h: Set with to Light Red Fill with Dark Red Text

steps.say: Prove it updates. Management raises the March target by forty lakh. In D13, type one crore fifty-eight lakh eighty thousand. Target achieved drops to ninety-nine point six percent and turns red; revenue and growth stay as they are.

Pro tip: keep each card's formula short and pointing at a single summary range. If the formula is long, build it in a helper cell first, then link the card to it. Readers trust numbers they can trace.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• One card = one number + one comparison
• Keep big numbers in ₹ lakh/crore format; round percentages to 1 decimal
• Card formulas point at summary cells, not long calculations

steps.say: On a Mac, Format Cells is Command 1 and the custom format box works the same. To type the triangle, press Control Command Space for the Character Viewer and search for triangle, or copy it from this lesson's sheet.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• ⌘ + 1 > Custom > Type
• ▲ ▼: Control + ⌘ + Space (Character Viewer), search 'triangle'
• Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules

steps.say: To recap: a card is a label, a number and a comparison. Use a three-part custom format for green and red arrows. Add a conditional format so missed targets turn red.

acts.t:
Recap

• SUM for the headline number
• [Color10]▲ 0.0%;[Red]▼ 0.0% for growth
• Conditional formatting for target status

steps.say: Your challenge: fill the fourth card in L3, March compared with February, with the same arrow format. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

L3: March revenue vs February, as ▲/▼ percent.

Answer: sheet S17-02 Done, cell F6

lessons.title: Pivot and slicer dashboard
lessons.mac:
• Insert > PivotTable, PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer
• Slicer tab > Report Connections
• Hide a sheet: Control-click the tab > Hide (Format > Sheet > Hide)
• Multi-select slicer buttons: ⌘ + click

steps.say: Managers love to click and filter. We'll build two PivotTables from the same sales table, revenue by region and by category, and control both with one financial-year slicer. Then we'll hide the raw data so the page looks clean.

acts.t:
Finished result

• S17-03!A3: PivotTable of Revenue by Region (Grand Total ₹25.99 crore, both years)
• S17-03!E3: PivotTable of Revenue by Category
• One FY slicer filters both
• SalesData sheet hidden
• Values-only copy on sheet S17-03 Done

steps.say: You will learn to place several PivotTables on one sheet, insert a slicer, connect it to every PivotTable, and hide the plumbing sheets. Practice sheet S17-03, data in table tblSales on SalesData.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Two PivotTables from tblSales on one sheet
2. Insert Slicer
3. Report Connections: one slicer, many pivots
4. Hide the data sheet

Practice: sheet S17-03

steps.say: A slicer is a set of buttons that filters a PivotTable. By default it controls only the PivotTable it was created from. Report Connections lets one slicer drive every PivotTable built on the same data.

acts.t:
Slicers

Insert Slicer → buttons for one field (FY)
Click a button = filter · Ctrl/⌘-click = several · Clear Filter icon = all
Report Connections → tick every PivotTable it should control
(PivotTables must share the same source)

steps.say: Go to sheet S17-03 and click A3. On the Insert tab, choose PivotTable, From Table or Range. Type tblSales as the range, choose Existing worksheet, location A3, and click OK.
In the field list, tick Region and then Revenue. Region goes to Rows and Revenue to Values automatically.
Click E3 and repeat: Insert, PivotTable, From Table or Range, tblSales, existing worksheet at E3. This time tick Category and Revenue.
Now the slicer. Click A4 inside the first PivotTable. On the PivotTable tab, click Insert Slicer, tick FY, and click OK.
Here is the common mistake. Click FY 2025-26 in the slicer. The region PivotTable filters, but the category PivotTable still shows both years. The two now disagree, which is worse than no filter.
With the slicer selected, go to the Slicer tab and click Report Connections. Tick PivotTable2 as well, and click OK. Now both PivotTables show financial year twenty-five twenty-six.
Click the Clear Filter button on the slicer to show both years again. The grand total is about twenty-six crore rupees across two years.
Finally, hide the plumbing. Go to SalesData, and on the Home tab choose Format, Hide and Unhide, Hide Sheet. The PivotTables still refresh from it; readers just don't see it.
Pro tip: give each PivotTable a number format through Value Field Settings, so the rupee format survives a refresh, and turn off the field buttons for a cleaner look.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• Value Field Settings > Number Format (₹ lakh format) - survives refresh
• PivotTable tab: turn off Field Headers / buttons
• Data > Refresh All after new data arrives

steps.say: On a Mac, PivotTables and slicers work the same. Report Connections is on the Slicer tab when the slicer is selected. To hide a sheet, Control-click its tab and choose Hide.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Insert > PivotTable, PivotTable Analyze > Insert Slicer
• Slicer tab > Report Connections
• Hide a sheet: Control-click the tab > Hide (Format > Sheet > Hide)
• Multi-select slicer buttons: ⌘ + click

steps.say: To recap: several PivotTables from one table, one slicer, and Report Connections so they agree. Hide the data sheet to keep the dashboard clean.

acts.t:
Recap

• Same source, several PivotTables
• Insert Slicer + Report Connections
• Clear Filter resets · hide plumbing sheets

steps.say: Your challenge: add a second slicer for Region, connect it to both PivotTables, and find the category revenue for financial year twenty-five twenty-six. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Add a Region slicer connected to both PivotTables.
With FY 2025-26 selected, what is revenue for each category?

Answer: sheet S17-03 Done, cell I3

lessons.title: Dynamic-array dashboard
lessons.mac:
• GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, TAKE, FILTER: Microsoft 365 for Mac (keep Excel updated)
• #NAME? on GROUPBY → Help > Check for Updates
• Data > Data Validation > List

steps.say: This dashboard has no PivotTables. Pick a region from the dropdown in B1 and every number, list and chart changes, all driven by a handful of formulas.
You will learn to add a region dropdown, total with FILTER, summarise with GROUPBY, handle a SPILL error, and chart the results. Practice sheet S17-04, data in tblSales.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Dropdown with Data Validation
2. SUM(FILTER()) for a KPI
3. GROUPBY for monthly, category and rep summaries
4. #SPILL! and charts on spilled ranges

Practice: sheet S17-04

steps.say: GROUPBY is a PivotTable in a formula: what to group by, what to add up, and how. The extra arguments switch off headers and totals, sort the result, and filter the rows first.

acts.t:
GROUPBY(row_fields, values, function, [field_headers], [total_depth], [sort_order], [filter_array])

row_fields: tblSales[Category]   values: tblSales[Revenue]   function: SUM
field_headers 0 = none · total_depth 0 = no total
sort_order -2 = by column 2, largest first
filter_array: (tblSales[Region]=$B$1)*(tblSales[FY]="FY 2025-26")

steps.say: First the dropdown. Select B1. On the Data tab click Data Validation, allow a List, and type the source North, South, East, West, separated by commas. Click OK, then type North in B1.
In B2, the headline number. Type equals SUM, open bracket, FILTER, open bracket, tblSales Revenue, comma.

Then the condition: open bracket, tblSales Region equals dollar B dollar one, close bracket, star, open bracket, tblSales FY equals FY 2025-26 in quotes, close bracket. The star means and. Close both brackets and press Return.

North sold three crore thirty-six lakh rupees in the year. Now the monthly trend. In A5, type equals GROUPBY of tblSales Month, tblSales Revenue, SUM, zero, zero, an empty sort, and the same filter. Press Return.
A5 shows the SPILL error. That's the classic dynamic-array mistake: GROUPBY needs twelve rows, and an old note in A12 is in the way. The dotted border shows where the answer wants to go.
Select A12 and press Delete. The twelve months spill down at once, already formatted as month and rupees.
In D5, revenue by category, sorted largest first with minus two: equals GROUPBY of tblSales Category, tblSales Revenue, SUM, zero, zero, minus two, and the filter.
In G5, the same for reps, so each region manager sees their team ranked.
Charts next. Select A5 to B16 and insert a line chart from the Insert tab. Then select D5 to E7 and insert a clustered bar chart. Drag them to the right of the tables.
Now the magic. Click B1 and choose South. The total, the monthly trend, the category ranking, the rep list and both charts all switch to South. South sold three crore eighty-eight lakh rupees.

Pro tip: these summaries always have twelve months, three categories and three reps, so the charts' ranges fit exactly. If a list can grow, chart a fixed maximum size, or use TAKE to limit it, for example the top five.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• Charts don't follow A5# automatically: keep summary sizes fixed
• Limit lists: =TAKE(GROUPBY(…,-2,…),5) for a top 5
• Keep the filter in one place (a helper cell or LET) to avoid typos

steps.say: On a Mac, GROUPBY needs a current Microsoft 365 build; it works exactly as here. Data Validation is on the Data tab. If GROUPBY shows a NAME error, update Excel from Help, Check for Updates.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, TAKE, FILTER: Microsoft 365 for Mac (keep Excel updated)
• #NAME? on GROUPBY → Help > Check for Updates
• Data > Data Validation > List

steps.say: To recap: one dropdown cell feeds every formula. FILTER gives KPIs, GROUPBY gives summary tables. Clear anything blocking a spill, and chart the spilled ranges.

acts.t:
Recap

• Data Validation dropdown = the dashboard's control
• SUM(FILTER()) and GROUPBY(…, filter_array)
• #SPILL! → clear the blocking cell

steps.say: Your challenge: below the dashboard, list the top three states for the year, for all regions, using TAKE and GROUPBY. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

In A19, show the top 3 states by FY 2025-26 revenue (all regions).
Hint: TAKE(GROUPBY(tblSales[State], …, -2, …), 3)

Answer: sheet S17-04 Done, cells A19:A20

lessons.title: Polishing: linked pictures, alignment and layout
learn: Linked picture for a live snapshot
lessons.mac:
• View (or Page Layout) tab: untick Gridlines, Headings
• Linked picture: ⌘ + C, then Home > Paste ▾ > Linked Picture
  (some builds: Edit > Paste Special > Linked Picture)
• Excel for the web cannot create linked pictures

steps.say: Same numbers, but this version looks like a report, not a spreadsheet: no gridlines, no row numbers, even spacing, and a live picture of the region table that updates whenever the data does.

You will learn to switch off gridlines and headings, use narrow spacer columns for even gaps, and paste a linked picture for a live snapshot. Practice sheets S17-05 and S17-05 Calc, recorded in Excel desktop because Excel for the web has no linked pictures.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Gridlines and headings off
2. Spacer columns for consistent gaps
3. Linked picture: a live snapshot of another range

Practice: sheets S17-05 and S17-05 Calc

steps.say: Three layout rules do most of the work. Remove anything that isn't data, like gridlines. Use the same gap everywhere, which narrow spacer columns give you. And line edges up with the cell grid.

acts.t:
Layout rules

• Remove clutter: gridlines, headings, extra borders
• Equal gaps: narrow spacer columns (width 2)
• Align to the grid: Alt-drag (Mac: ⌘-drag) snaps objects to cell edges
• Linked picture = live image of a range from another sheet

steps.say: Here is the rough version on sheet S17-05. On the View tab, untick Gridlines and then Headings. The sheet already looks calmer.
Now spacing. Select columns A, C, D, F and G together, and on the Home tab choose Format, Column Width. Type two and click OK. These become the gaps.
Select columns B, E and H, the card columns, and set them all to eighteen. Every card is now the same width with the same gap.
Now the region table from the Calc sheet. Go to S17-05 Calc, select A1 to C6 and press Command C.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S17-05 Calc

steps.say: The common mistake is a normal paste. Back on S17-05, select K3 and press Command V. The cells land with their own column widths and break the layout, and the formulas point at the wrong cells. Press Command Z.
Instead, with K3 still selected, open the Paste arrow on the Home tab and choose Linked Picture. You get an image of the table that floats over the cells, so it doesn't care about column widths.

It's live. A late order for East was missing. Go to S17-05 Calc, and in B4 type four crore twenty lakh. Back on the dashboard, the picture updates, total revenue becomes fifteen crore twelve lakh, and the best region card now says East.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S17-05 Calc

steps.say: Pro tip: to line up a chart with the cards, hold Alt on Windows, or Command on a Mac, while you drag its edge. It snaps to the cell borders. For several objects, use Shape Format, Align.

acts.t:
Pro tip: alignment

• Drag with Alt (Mac: ⌘) to snap to cell edges
• Select several objects > Shape Format > Align > Align Left / Distribute
• Format pane > Properties: 'Don't move or size with cells' for fixed layouts

steps.say: On a Mac, untick Gridlines and Headings on the View tab or the Page Layout tab. For a linked picture, copy the range, then on the Home tab open the Paste arrow and choose Linked Picture; on some builds it is Edit, Paste Special, Linked Picture.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• View (or Page Layout) tab: untick Gridlines, Headings
• Linked picture: ⌘ + C, then Home > Paste ▾ > Linked Picture
  (some builds: Edit > Paste Special > Linked Picture)
• Excel for the web cannot create linked pictures

steps.say: To recap: hide gridlines and headings, use spacer columns for equal gaps, and snap objects to the grid. Use a linked picture to show a live snapshot from another sheet.

acts.t:
Recap

• Gridlines and headings off
• Spacer columns = consistent gaps
• Linked Picture = live snapshot that ignores column widths

steps.say: Your challenge: line up the chart's left edge with the first card and its right edge with the third card. How do you make it snap? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Align the chart edges with column B (left) and column H (right).

Answer: sheet S17-05 Done, cell K20

lessons.title: Project: sales performance dashboard
learn: From raw data to a one-page dashboard
lessons.mac:
• Same formulas and menus in Excel for Microsoft 365 on Mac
• GROUPBY/TAKE need a current build (Help > Check for Updates)
• ⌘ + 1 for formats · Share button top-right

steps.say: This is the project: a one-page sales performance dashboard for financial year twenty-five twenty-six. Four KPI cards, a monthly trend, a category split and the top reps, all switchable by region from one dropdown, and ready to share.

We'll use everything from this section: KPI formulas, a dropdown, GROUPBY summaries, charts and polish. Practice sheet S17-06, with the raw data in tblSales and targets in tblTarget on the SalesData sheet.

acts.t:
Project build

1. Title and Region dropdown (All + 4 regions)
2. KPI cards: Revenue, Growth, Units, Target achieved
3. GROUPBY: monthly trend, categories, top 5 reps
4. Two charts, gridlines off, test, share

Practice: sheet S17-06 · data: tblSales, tblTarget

steps.say: Start from the questions, not the chart types. How much did we sell? Are we growing? Did we hit target? Which months, products and people drive it? Each question becomes one card or one table.

acts.t:
Questions → dashboard parts

How much did we sell?         → Revenue card
Are we growing?                  → Growth vs FY 2024-25 card
How much volume?               → Units card
Did we hit target?              → Target achieved card
When? What? Who?              → Monthly trend · Category split · Top 5 reps
Can each manager see theirs? → Region dropdown

steps.say: Go to sheet S17-06. In A1, type the title, Sales Performance Dashboard, colon, FY 2025-26.

acts.h: Type Sales Performance Dashboard: FY 2025-26 and press Return

steps.say: B2 is the control. On the Data tab, add Data Validation with a List: All, North, South, East, West. Then type All in B2.

Revenue card in B5: SUMIFS of tblSales Revenue, where FY is FY 2025-26, and Region matches IF B2 is All, then a star, else B2. The star is a wildcard that matches every region, which is how All works.
Growth card in D5: B5 divided by the same SUMIFS for FY 2024-25, minus one. The arrow format from the KPI lesson is already applied.
Units card in F5: the same SUMIFS as revenue, but on the Units column.
Target card in H5: B5 divided by the target. If B2 is All, use the sum of all targets; otherwise XLOOKUP the region's target from tblTarget.
Colour the target card: Home, Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Less Than one, with light red fill. The company is at a hundred and one point seven percent, so it stays plain for now.

acts.h: Set with to Light Red Fill with Dark Red Text

steps.say: Now the category table, and a mistake to watch for. In D9, GROUPBY with the filter tblSales Region equals B2. Press Return, and you get a CALC error: no row has a region called All, so the result is empty.
Fix it with the same IF trick. When B2 is All, the region test becomes one, which keeps every row. Retype D9 with IF B2 equals All, one, else the region test.
In A9, the monthly trend: GROUPBY of tblSales Month and Revenue, with no sort, and the same corrected filter. Twelve months spill down.
In G9, the top five reps: TAKE, open bracket, GROUPBY by Rep sorted largest first, with the filter, then comma five. Lakshmi Iyer leads with one crore thirty-one lakh rupees.
Add the charts. Select A9 to B20 and insert a line chart. Select D9 to E11 and insert a clustered bar chart. Drag both to the right of the tables.
Polish it: on the View tab, untick Gridlines. The cards, tables and charts now read as one page, top to bottom, the order a manager asks the questions.
Test it like a user. Choose South in B2. Revenue becomes three crore eighty-eight lakh, and the trend, categories, reps and charts follow. Then set it back to All.

Ready to share. Hide the SalesData sheet, protect the dashboard sheet so only B2 can change, and share a link with Can view, or Can edit for managers who use the dropdown. Check the numbers against a quick PivotTable once before you send it.

acts.t:
Ready to share

☐ Hide SalesData (Control-click tab > Hide)
☐ Unlock B2, Review > Protect Sheet
☐ Check one total against a PivotTable
☐ Share > link: Can view (or Can edit for the dropdown)
☐ Optional: File > Export > PDF for the monthly email

steps.say: On a Mac, everything here works in Excel for Microsoft 365: SUMIFS, XLOOKUP, GROUPBY and TAKE, Data Validation and the charts. Keep Excel updated so GROUPBY is available, and share from the Share button at the top right.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Same formulas and menus in Excel for Microsoft 365 on Mac
• GROUPBY/TAKE need a current build (Help > Check for Updates)
• ⌘ + 1 for formats · Share button top-right

steps.say: To recap: start from the questions, build one card or table per question, drive everything from one dropdown, and test every option before you share.

acts.t:
Recap

• Questions → KPIs → layout
• SUMIFS + "*" wildcard for All; IF(…="All",1,…) inside GROUPBY filters
• Charts on fixed-size spills · test · share

steps.say: Your challenge: select West and write down the four KPI values. Is West above or below target? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Set B2 to West. Record Revenue, Growth, Units and Target achieved.
Is West above or below target?

Answer: sheet S17-06 Done, cell A23
